issues.description: Inconsistent description of what the second returned list from build_msd_circ represents. The problem statement requires the second list to correspond to the destructive measurements of the 15 qubits of the tetrahedral code (i.e., the 15 code-qubit measurement indices). The template's docstring (and its wording) describes the return as the "final X-basis measurements of the distilled state" (singular), which could be read as referring to the distilled qubit rather than the 15 code qubits. The solution implementation returns a list corresponding to the 15 code-qubit measurements. This mismatch in the docstring/description vs. the problem text can confuse students about what the function should return and in what order the indices should appear.
issues.suggested_fix: Unify the wording so all artifacts explicitly state the same thing. For example: "The function returns (telemetry_measurements, code_qubit_measurements) where the second list contains the 15 measurement indices for the tetrahedral code qubits (in ascending qubit order)." Update the template docstring to match the problem statement and the solution implementation.

issues.description: Type mismatch for the batch_size parameter of simulate_msd_two_rounds between the problem statement and the code. The problem statement signature uses batch_size: float = 1000000.0, while both the template and the solution define simulate_msd_two_rounds(..., batch_size: int = 1000000). This inconsistency in type annotation may confuse students about whether batch_size should be an integer number of shots (which is appropriate) or a float.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the batch_size annotation consistent across all artifacts. Prefer using an integer type (batch_size: int) in the problem statement, template, and solution, since batch size represents a number of shots. Update the problem statement signature to batch_size: int = 1000000.
